SMTO-WEB-0030 — An older record warns the item you named may have been swapped

GUID: 18f81cba-56aa-5b02-ac97-6ffbbd56fd0b
Slug: research-exact-identifier-not-preserved
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • This message comes from an older saved record. It warns that a product or reference you named may have been replaced with a similar one. Today's SMTO asks you instead of swapping.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read the latest answer and check that it names exactly the product, model number or code you asked about. This message is from an older record, so your current answer may already be correct.
  2. If the answer talks about a different item, reply with the exact name or code, and say that similar items are not acceptable. SMTO keeps the exact name you give and asks you before considering anything else.
  3. If SMTO asks you which item you meant, answer that question in the conversation. Your answer is what allows SMTO to use a different item when the name is ambiguous.

What success looks like

  • The answer is about exactly the item you named, or SMTO asks you to confirm an alternative.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting where you saw this message. Don't treat this older message alone as proof that the current answer swapped your item.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Retained catalog alias research_exact_identifier_not_preserved: a saved diagnostic reports an unverified identifier substitution; current code has no emitting site and handles exact entities through unresolved-identity and clarification paths.

What this means

  • This retained alias describes an exact identifier being substituted, but current entity handling uses explicit unresolved-identity and clarification paths instead of emitting this alias. This retained catalog alias has no direct current emitting site. The related runtime behavior supplies context only; the alias alone does not establish that the check ran, publication was blocked, or a model call failed.

Why this can happen

  • This retained alias describes an exact identifier being substituted, but current entity handling uses explicit unresolved-identity and clarification paths instead of emitting this alias.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the user's literal identifier with retained entity resolution and the original emitting version.

How to fix it

  • Treat as historical: locate where the diagnostic was recorded before acting. Current research preserves exact_entities verbatim (validate_answer prefixes 'Requested: ...' when missing) and blocks identity-dependent answers with research_entity_clarification_required; resolve ambiguity through that clarification flow, never by silent substitution.
  • Preserve the exact requested identifier and resolve ambiguity through the current entity clarification flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • The requested identity is preserved or an explicit user clarification authorizes the alternative.

What not to do

  • Do not silently replace an exact identifier or infer a current substitution solely from a retained diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • This retained catalog alias has no direct current emitting site. The related runtime behavior supplies context only; the alias alone does not establish that the check ran, publication was blocked, or a model call failed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
